Hi Jordan — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I’ve attached a CSV with the quick benchmark rows we ran on your sample data and a one-pager with the JSON schema examples.

Call summary (2-line): Acme wants deterministic structured outputs for claims triage, occasional tool calls to your case-management API, and strict auditability. Primary concerns: schema drift/regression across model updates and retry behavior when tool-calls fail.

Recommended short-list (models to evaluate, prioritized):
- redwood-l1-7b-quant (fast, low-latency, good structured-output stability)
- llama-3-13b-8k (higher quality for ambiguous prompts; may need quantization)
- mosaic-mpt-7b-xl (cheap baseline for simple rules)

Quick acceptance criteria we propose for the POC:
- JSON schema compliance >= 98% on 1k sample prompts (strict key presence + types).
- Tool-call success rate >= 99% with idempotent request pattern (for duplicate delivery).
- Semantic accuracy (label-level) >= 92% on your hand-labeled set.
- Mean token cost per request < $0.015 (configurable via batching/quantization).
- P95 latency < 500ms (edge cases excluded).

Evaluation artifacts and links:
- Benchmarks: Google Drive (see attached CSV) — contains per-model token/time/cost rows.
- Notebook: https://notebooks.redwood.ai/acme-eval-2028 (live eval harness + prompt sets).
- Prompt sets included in attachment: acme-prompt-sets.zip (30 rule-based + 200 edge-case prompts).

Structured output & function-calling notes:
- We'll surface generates as a JSON payload and validate against a typed JSON Schema before downstream processing. If the schema validation fails, we will trigger a deterministic fallback flow (1) attempt a repair prompt + re-run inference, (2) if still invalid, create an automated case for human review and return a stable error response to the caller.
- Recommended validation thresholds: automatic repair attempts limited to 1 per request. Repair prompt should include the failing output and the schema excerpt (see attached one-pager).

Retries and idempotency guidance (short):
- Client-facing retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter; initial delay 200ms, backoff factor 2, max retries 3.
- For tool-calls: always include an idempotency token (UUID) and server-side dedup window 60s.

Jordan — adding implementation specifics you can hand to your engineering team.

Function-calling payload & validation flow (high level):
1) LLM returns: {
   \"outcome\": "triage",
   \"triage_reason\": "policy_violation",
   \"confidence\": 0.93,
   \"case\": {
     \"external_id\": "AC-12345",
     \"priority\": "high"
   }
}

2) We run a JSON Schema validator that checks required keys and types. Example schema excerpt (human-readable):
- outcome: enum [triage, close, escalate] (string)
- triage_reason: string maxLength 256
- confidence: number between 0 and 1
- case.external_id: string (pattern ^[A-Z0-9-]+$)
- case.priority: enum [low, medium, high]

On validation error: call repair_prompt(), which does:
- POST to Redwood inference with body: {
  prompt: repair_instructions + failing_output + schema_snippet,
  model: redwood-l1-7b-quant,
  max_tokens: 256
}

Retry strategy (tool-calls & external webhooks):
- Client/backoff: initial=200ms, factor=2, jitter=50-150ms, max_retries=3. After 3 failures mark as DELIVERY_FAILED and open a ticket.
- Server-side dedup: accept idempotency-token header, persist tokens for 60s; if duplicate seen, return 200 with previous result id.
- If repair_prompt returns "REPAIR_FAILED" open a human-review case automatically (attach raw output + model logits snapshot).

Observability & regression detection:
- Per-commit/rollout: run full 1k prompt set as smoke test with diff metrics (schema pass rate, semantic accuracy, token-cost delta). Block rollout if schema pass rate drops by more than 1.5% or semantic accuracy drops > 3 points.
- Keep model-versioned artifacts (prompt seeds, random seeds, tokenizer state) for reproducibility.

Sample curl for function call (idempotent request):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6" \
  -d '{\n    "model":"redwood-l1-7b-quant",\n    "input":"<repair:validate against schema>..."\n  }'

Let me know if you want the sample validator code (JS/Python) — I can push a small repo.
